title: DATETIME2 Data Type
description: Learn how to use the DATETIME2 data type to store both date and time data.

data.text: The DATETIME2 data type stores both date and time data. It is the recommended type for new applications over the older DATETIME type.

data.title: DATETIME2 Syntax
data.content: Defines a DATETIME2 column with optional fractional seconds precision.

data.text: The fractional seconds precision is optional, ranging from 0 to 7. Storage size varies: 6 bytes for precision less than 3, 7 bytes for precision 3-4, and 8 bytes for all other precisions.

data.title: Create DATETIME2 Column

data.title: Default DATETIME2 Value
data.content: Sets the default value of created_at to the current date and time.

data.text: `DATETIME2(p)` accepts a precision from 0 to 7 fractional digits. Lower precision means less storage: `DATETIME2(0)` uses 6 bytes, `DATETIME2(3)` uses 7, and the default `DATETIME2(7)` uses 8. If you do not need sub-second accuracy, declare the precision explicitly.

data.title: Current time at several precisions
data.content: `SYSDATETIME()` returns the full precision of the platform clock, and each CAST rounds it to the destination precision.

data.title: Interview answer
data.text: Say that `DATETIME2` replaced `DATETIME` because it has a larger date range (0001-01-01 to 9999-12-31), higher accuracy (100 ns vs about 3.33 ms), and follows the ANSI SQL standard. Store timestamps in UTC and convert for display.

data.title: DATETIME2 Key Points
points: DATETIME2 stores both date and time with fractional seconds precision.
Precision ranges from 0 to 7, with storage from 6 to 8 bytes.
Use DATETIME2 instead of DATETIME for new applications.
The default string format is YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss[.fractional seconds].
CURRENT_TIMESTAMP can be used as a default value.
